sections.label: G20 growth after crisis
sections.summary: Seven years after the Global Financial Crisis, G20 growth is 3.2% per annum versus 4.1% before the crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Seven years after the Global Financial Crisis, G20 economic growth is still lower than before the crisis, at 3.2% per annum versus 4.1% per annum before the crisis.

sections.label: G20 job shortfall
sections.summary: Across G20 countries, there is said to be a shortfall of 50 million jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Across the G20 countries, there is said to be a shortfall of 50 million jobs.

sections.label: Falling workforce growth
sections.summary: Workforce growth is falling from 4% per year earlier in the decade to around 1% per year by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Workforce growth is falling from 4% per year in the earlier part of the decade, to around 1% per year by 2020.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Singapore agency
sections.summary: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) is the new agency tasked with this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) is the new agency tasked with this.

sections.label: WSG support for SMEs
sections.summary: WSG will help SMEs and firm clusters become manpower-lean and innovative, redesign jobs, improve HR practices, develop e-services and career fairs, and use data analytics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: WSG will also pay attention to small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: It will continue to help companies and clusters of firms to become more manpower-lean and innovative, such as through the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: In addition, it will work with businesses to redesign jobs and improve human resource (HR) practices so that they can turn their human resources into human capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Beyond physical touch points, WSG will develop new service models, such as e-services and online career fairs, and also provide timely and customised information and career guidance to individuals at different stages of their career.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: It will also move towards leveraging data analytics and smart technology to find new ways to optimise matching between jobseekers and employers.

sections.label: Retrenchment numbers
sections.summary: Retrenchments were 15,580 for 2015 and exceeded 20,000 in the last four quarters, with over 10,000 in the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Retrenchments were at 15,580 for 2015 and in the last four quarters alone have exceeded the 20,000 mark, with more than 10,000 contributed in the first half of this year.

sections.label: Residents laid off were PMETs
sections.summary: Of the 9,090 residents laid off last year, 71% were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Last year, among the 9,090 residents laid off, 71% were PMETs.

sections.label: PCPs filled, CSP awareness lacking
sections.summary: Some advertised PCPs in sectors like social services and healthcare are full, and awareness of the Career Support Programme is lacking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: From my NTUC's U PME Centre team, I also know that some of the advertised PCPs in certain sectors, such as social services and 	Page: 32 healthcare are already completely filled and not taking in more Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, the Career Support Programme (CSP) is a good scheme to incentivise employers to hire PMEs especially those above 40 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, I feel there is a general lack of awareness by employers and PMEs alike on CSP despite it being implemented since October last year and further enhanced after the Committee of Supply debate this year.

sections.label: NTUC Career Activation Programme pilot
sections.summary: NTUC piloted a Career Activation Programme last year providing emotional and confidence building through volunteer career activists who had been laid off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The National Trade Unions Congress (NTUC) piloted a Career Activation Programme last year where we provide emotional and confidence building through a peer support network of volunteers who themselves have been through layoffs and are now in good jobs, whom we call career activists.

sections.label: New clause on workforce research
sections.summary: The amendment Bill inserts a clause to promote or undertake research in Singapore into matters relating to the Singapore workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, a new clause is inserted by virtue of the amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is "to promote or undertake research in Singapore into matters relating to the Singapore workforce." I have articulated in this House before on more than one occasion and am urging again for WSG to undertake a research study into non-time-based underemployment in Singapore so that we are able to ascertain whether there is, indeed, this situation in Singapore with more Singaporeans being higher skilled and higher educated.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow, underemployment
sections.summary: The Adapt and Grow Programme and PCP should be more responsive, relevant, flexible and comprehensive, and MOM should address underemployment of highly educated people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, the Adapt and Grow Programme and the PCP should be more responsive, relevant, flexible and comprehensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, I urge MOM to pay attention to the underemployment situation for highly educated people.

sections.label: Australia JobActive job placements
sections.summary: Australia's JobActive Programme has achieved more than 200,000 job placements since July 2015, linking jobseekers with job network providers given cash incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In Australia, for example, the JobActive Programme has achieved more than 200,000 job placements since it was started in July 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: They link jobseekers with job network providers that are based in 1,700 locations across the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These providers are given cash incentives for successful matching.

sections.label: Quota for EP holders
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister would consider a targeted quota for Employment Pass holders in high growth and strategic sectors like IT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: To help WSG in its mission, rather than a blunt broad sectoral approach, would the Minister also consider a more nuanced and targeted approach – implementing a quota for EP holders, especially in high growth and strategic sectors like IT?

sections.label: WSG responsibilities after restructuring
sections.summary: States that after restructuring, WSG will build the Singaporean Core, help enterprises stay competitive, and avoid over-reliance on manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After restructuring, WSG will be responsible for building the Singaporean Core in the workforce for all trades and industries, assist enterprises to maintain their competitiveness, and not have an over-reliance on manpower.

sections.label: MNCs, large enterprises, SMEs
sections.summary: Notes that MNCs and large enterprises appeal most to job-seekers, while traditional industries and SMEs need WSG's help most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Multinational corporations (MNCs) and large enterprises have always had the greatest appeal to job-seekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those which need WSG's help most are the traditional industries and SMEs.

sections.label: SMEs and automation machines
sections.summary: Gives the example that SMEs can buy machines under mechanisation and automation efforts but have no use for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the Government encourages enterprises to mechanise and automate; SMEs can buy the machines but have no use for them.

sections.label: WSG steering enterprises
sections.summary: Says that with WSG, a specific Government agency will steer enterprises towards creating good job opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the setting up of WSG, there will be a specific Government agency to steer enterprises towards creating good job opportunities for Singaporeans, and I hope that with everyone pitching in to work hard, the situation could be changed for the better.

sections.label: WDA reorganisation as WSG
sections.summary: States the Bill reorganises WDA as WSG, refocuses its functions, and requires WSG to collaborate with SSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With what has been termed the "Fourth Industrial Revolution", Singapore, together with many countries globally, is experiencing disruptive changes to business models which are having a profound impact on jobs and employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is therefore timely that the Singapore Workforce Development Agency (Amendment) Bill seeks to reorganise the WDA as WSG and refocus its functions and duties to enable Singaporeans to have quality jobs and careers and to ensure that organisations can become more manpower-lean and remain competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This change in alignment with the formation of SSG, a new Statutory Board under MOE taking over WDA's functions of adult continuing education and training and the promotion of lifelong learning and the administration of Skills Development Fund, will still require the new WSG to work in close collaboration with SSG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that clause 9 calls out explicitly the expectation for WSG to, quote, "cooperate and collaborate with the proposed SSG", as it "discharges its function under the SkillsFuture Singapore Agency Bill 2016 when enacted".

sections.label: WSG and HR best practices
sections.summary: Rapid change affects skills for current and new roles, and WSG's clause 9 function includes promoting HR best practices in recruitment, training, development and talent management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The rapid pace of change and business model disruptions are simultaneously impacting skills required for both current and emerging new roles across different industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is positive that one of the key functions of WSG as indicated in clause 9 is promoting and facilitating the adoption of human resources (HR) best practices, that is, focusing on recruitment, training, development and managing talent.

sections.label: Labour disruption impact on women
sections.summary: A World Economic Forum study reported labour disruptions will disproportionately hurt women, so WSG should work with companies to tap women's talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum's Industry Gender Gap Study, the first study of its kind representing more than 13 million employees in nine industry sectors and 15 economies has reported that labour disruptions that we have been discussing will have a disproportionate negative impact on women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This may be explained in part by the fact that the roles most at risk from automation and disintermediation are held in larger proportion by women or that women are relatively under-represented in jobs that are expected to have the most potential for growth, for example, in computing and engineering; and that women will still make up a smaller share of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is therefore imperative that WSG works with companies to tackle barriers to tapping the talent pool of women, given that we, in Singapore especially, have a highly educated and skilled female population in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It will also require individuals to be proactive in learning and owning their careers, and companies to actively invest in tapping all segments of their workforce in training and re-skilling in order to be able to take advantage of new opportunities and to stay competitive.

sections.label: WSG employability objectives
sections.summary: Clause 9 objectives include helping Singapore Citizens and residents find and keep jobs and working with employers to promote industry-specific skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For clause 9, I am particularly heartened that among the objectives of WSG is to help Singapore Citizens and residents be employable through services and facilities to help them find and keep jobs, and also by working closely with employers and other relevant commerce or public sector agencies to identify and promote the enhancement of industry-specific skills.

sections.label: Help for retrenched PMEs
sections.summary: In a challenging employment market, the speaker hopes employment assistance will also help PMEs in their 40s and 50s who lost jobs despite upgrading courses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is especially so in the current challenging employment market.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that such employment assistance will not be confined to just blue-collar workers or para-professionals and that PMEs will also be provided help, including PMEs who are in their 40s or 50s.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For the past six months or so, through house visits and Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS), I have met increasingly more PMEs, especially those in their 40s and 50s who have lost their jobs, been retrenched and could not find employment thereafter, even though they have taken up upgrading courses.

sections.label: Support for WDA Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Singapore Workforce Development Agency (Amendment) Bill and commends transferring WDA's education and training role to a new agency.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Page: 38 Mdm Speaker, notwithstanding this few suggestions that I have, I fully support the Singapore Workforce Development Agency (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I commend the move to transfer WDA's previously held role in education and training to a new agency.

sections.label: Productivity help for businesses
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister what else the Ministry will do to help businesses with no or little substitute for human workers increase productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Beyond job redesign, however, I would like to ask the Minister what else the Ministry will be doing to help businesses for which there is no or little substitute for human workers, to increase their productivity.

sections.label: Randstad survey on Singaporean satisfaction
sections.summary: Randstad surveys consistently rank Singaporeans among the least satisfied workforces in the Asia-Pacific.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Surveys by Randstad consistently place Singaporeans as one of the least satisfied workforces in the Asia-Pacific.

sections.label: Question on new agency
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister whether the new agency will address negative workplace satisfaction survey results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Minister if the new agency will look into how we can turn the tide of these negative survey results on workplace satisfaction.

sections.label: 2014 survey on flexible work
sections.summary: A 2014 survey showed 47% of Singapore companies offer at least one form of flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A survey in 2014 showed that 47% of companies in Singapore offer at least one form of flexible work arrangements.

sections.label: Flexible hours for full-time workers
sections.summary: Only 12% of companies offer flexible work hours for people who want to work full-time.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For people who want to work full-time, only 12% of companies offer flexible work hours.

sections.label: Use of flexible arrangements
sections.summary: A 2014 survey showed about 15% of workers use long-term flexible arrangements, and Singaporeans work 44.3 hours weekly.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another survey in 2014 showed that, of the companies that offer flexible working arrangements, only about 15% of workers make use of long-term flexible arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many employees feel that they have to be in the office until the bosses leave the office.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We work, on average, 44.3 hours a week, and that is 50% more than the Germans.

sections.label: Extending PCP to more sectors
sections.summary: Mid-career workers affected by restructuring prompt speeding up extension of PCP to more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: At the same time, we also recognise that with the faster pace of restructuring, many of them in their mid-career will be affected even more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is the reason why we will speed up the process of extending PCP to even more sectors, as the Member Mr Patrick Tay mentioned, in terms of how we can be more responsive and flexible.

sections.label: SME support via LED scheme
sections.summary: Support for SMEs has been stepped up with the Lean Enterprise Development scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the case of SMEs, we have stepped up our support for SMEs with the Lean Enterprise Development (LED) scheme.

sections.label: New central kitchen for Indian restaurants
sections.summary: A new central kitchen was opened two weeks ago for this group of Indian restaurants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Just two weeks ago, we opened up a new central kitchen for this group of Indian restaurants.

sections.label: Ten restaurants share central kitchen
sections.summary: Under the LED scheme, 10 restaurants jointly invest in a central kitchen, improving productivity and minimising manpower needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Under the LED scheme, we brought them together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: These 10 restaurants jointly invest in this central kitchen and, as a result, they are now able to improve their productivity, and at the same time, minimise their manpower requirement.

sections.label: Three flexi-work thrusts in Singapore
sections.summary: Flexi-work arrangements in Singapore focus on flexi-place, flexi-time and flexi-load.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In Singapore today, under flexi-work arrangements, we focus on three thrusts: first, flexi-place, including working from home; second, flexi-time, including starting work two hours earlier, ending work two hours earlier; and third, flexi-load so that a person can decide whether I want to have a 100% load, 50% or 75% and so on.

sections.label: RFID installed under LED scheme
sections.summary: Under the LED scheme, help is given to install radio-frequency identification in all sales items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Under the LED scheme, we help them to install radio-frequency identification (RFID) in all their sales items.

sections.label: Redefined EP framework scrutiny
sections.summary: The EP framework was redefined to look at the industry and company, with closer scrutiny of triple weak companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As I mentioned in Parliament in the Committee of Supply debate this year, we have already redefined our EP framework not just to look at the qualification of individual EP applicants, but also to look at the industry, to look at the company and, along the way, we provide closer scrutiny to what we call the "triple weak" companies.

sections.label: Ageing local workforce, slowing growth
sections.summary: The passage states the local workforce is ageing and growth is slowing from 4% a year in the first half of the decade to about 1% by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This is one of the key challenges we face moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I have said it time and time again that our local workforce is ageing and growth is slowing down very rapidly – from growing at 4% a year in the first half of the decade this year to about 1% by 2020, which is just about four or five years from now.

sections.label: WSG, MOM sectoral HR plan
sections.summary: The passage states this is a top priority of MOM and tripartite partners, and that a sectoral plan for human resource has been formulated and is being formalised, launched and implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In that regard, I would say that this will be more than just a priority of WSG, but one of the top priorities of MOM, together with the tripartite partners as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We have formulated the sectoral plan for human resource.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: We are now in the process of formalising it, launching it and getting it implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: At the G20 Labour and Employment meeting, having expressed the concern with this slower economic growth, slower job growth, the conclusion amongst our G20 Labour Ministers is that we have to ensure that this innovation growth will be as fast as possible, as smart as possible.
